title: CVE Program: common vulnerability identifiers as software negative-space naming infrastructure
summary: CVE is encoded as a naming rail. It gives publicly disclosed vulnerabilities stable shared identifiers, which lets later records connect advisories, scanners, exploits, patches, incidents, and postmortems without treating the identifier itself as mitigation.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0010 as vulnerability/source-infrastructure rail for the software failure lane.

claims.claim: The CVE Program’s official source-index states that CVE identifies, defines, and catalogs publicly disclosed cybersecurity vulnerabilities; NVD explains that CVEs are unique identifiers that let multiple parties refer to the same vulnerability and associate code versions.
what_would_change_status: CVE Program or NVD changes the stated role of CVE identifiers.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: NVD describes CVE as a dictionary/glossary maintained by MITRE and sponsored by DHS/CISA, with CNAs assigning identifiers; NVD also notes that MITRE and CNAs do not patch or mitigate vulnerabilities.
what_would_change_status: Governance or role statements change materially.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official/institutional source extraction; no coverage or outcome audit
limitations: Establishes infrastructure existence and declared function only.
Does not claim completeness, timeliness, exploit prevalence, patch compliance, or incident-prevention effect.

reporter_protection_design: not evaluated in rev0010; CVE assignment is not a confidential incident-reporting channel
outputs: references used by downstream repositories and advisories
limitations: coverage/timeliness vary by disclosure and assignment process
type_payload.query_value: Lets the cube link a breach or outage to a named vulnerability without confusing vulnerability naming with remediation.

handling_notes: Vulnerability infrastructure records should not become exploit catalogues; keep to identifier, enrichment, prioritization, and remediation-governance roles.
Do not infer patch status, exploitation, or blame from mere presence/absence in a vulnerability catalog without record-specific evidence.

unknowns: Coverage, timeliness, enrichment lag, and real remediation effects are not audited.
Dynamic/403/source-index pages need archive/API pass where relevant.
next_actions: Sample records to test identifier-to-patch-to-incident linkage.
Create negative-control cases where vulnerability rails worked and incidents were averted.

revision_history.change: Claim support migrated to typed evidence_refs; factual claim text and statuses unchanged.
